title: Add a new content operand while keeping mechanisms fixed
hypothesis: A new what/content vector encoded by a small Mirror code can be composed with frozen known how/operators to produce heldout outputs at lower total bytes and no worse retention than adding an explicit native operand vector or retraining the shared core.

world.teacher: fixed operator matrices act on content vectors; new content lies in a frozen rank-2 shared content basis

fresh.release_rule: Keep fresh sealed on exact native content-code alias or full-byte gate failure.

controls: frozen shared what basis plus Mirror code

paid_objects: new what code or explicit vector

success_gate: new-what heldout nRMSE <=0.02, old-what retention nRMSE <=0.02, at least 25% fewer total bytes than explicit operand and strict gain over native coordinate code.
failure_gate: FAIL if native code exactly matches Mirror or full bytes fail frozen gate.
boundaries: Synthetic linear computations only; no continual-learning or reasoning claim.
Frozen operator family and content basis are known synthetic controls.
No audit seeds after development alias or gate failure.
